title: substance-catalog substance entry
description: One compound. Reference data only: this file describes a substance, never a person, and contains no health data. Every asserted value carries evidence pointing at a row in `sources`.

key.description: Stable slug. NEVER changes once published — the app's intervention.substance_key points at it. Matches the human-system bulk-import slug pattern.

name.description: Canonical display name, normally the INN / USAN generic name.

aka.description: Brand names, common synonyms, and research codes. Not a search index — only names a person would plausibly write down.

class.description: Pharmacological class in prose, e.g. 'GLP-1 / GIP dual agonist'. Free text by design: no ATC, no closed vocabulary.

category.description: Coarse bucket the app groups the stack by. One only.

regulatory_status.description: US regulatory footing. fda_approved = an approved product with an FDA label. rx_compounded = obtained through compounding rather than an approved product. research_chemical = sold for laboratory use only, no human-use approval. otc_supplement = marketed as a dietary supplement. unscheduled = neither approved nor controlled, outside the supplement framework. study_only = investigational, in trials, no marketing authorisation.

typical_dose_shape.description: The SHAPE of a dose — magnitude, unit, cadence — so the UI can render a slider and sanity-check a typed dose. It is not a recommendation and is not personalised. Omit or null it where no honest range exists.

description.description: Factual and descriptive. States what the compound is and what it is approved or used for. NEVER advisory — no 'should', no 'recommended', no dosing counsel.

systems.description: Body systems this compound touches, and how. Exactly one relation per (system, relation) pair.

monitors.description: 'Taking this requires watching marker Y every N days.' marker_key must resolve against data/marker-keys.json.

sources.description: Every source any value in this file came from. The licence gate runs over these.

source_gaps.description: Lookups that were run and returned NOTHING. Recorded rather than silently omitted, so an empty result is distinguishable from a source never consulted.

valid_from.description: AIRAC-style effectivity start. The first bundle date on which this row is in force.

valid_to.description: Effectivity end, or null for 'in force until superseded'. Must be strictly after valid_from.

systemKey.description: The thirteen human-system body systems a fresh install seeds. Nothing else is accepted HERE, deliberately: the app resolves a system key against its own database and can hold more, but a catalog bundle is published once and read by every install, so it may only name keys every install has. `skin` and `hair` were added 2026-08-25 and are two systems rather than one integumentary system, because the app's load cap is two live acts_on per system and a finasteride + minoxidil + retinoid stack is three, treating two unrelated things.

relation.description: acts_on = the system the compound is INTENDED to affect, placed by intended effect and never by signalling pathway. burdens = a system the compound stresses, is cleared by, or carries a toxicity signal against. confounds = a system whose MARKERS this compound distorts without acting on it. The app collapses burdens and confounds to its own `monitors` relation; only acts_on counts against the load cap.

evidence.description: One or more source ids from this file's `sources`.

why.description: Why this marker, in one sentence. Surfaced in the app's alert explanation chain.

evidenceId.description: Namespaced id that MUST equal the `id` of a row in this file's `sources`.

license.description: THE LICENCE GATE. This enum is the allowlist. Anything outside it fails validation and the build, by design — an unclean licence in this repo is what makes the curation unsaleable. Do not widen it to make a row pass.
